subject: Chemistry
schema_note: Keyed by topic_id (matches chemistry_syllabus_jee_main.json). Same field set as the Physics NCERT-context file: 'hard_archetypes' calibrated to JEE-Main-level difficulty (single/dual-concept, not the multi-topic fusion typical of Advanced) and 'banned_easy_templates' generally left as a note that direct-substitution/direct-recall questions are wanted, not excluded, since that is the opposite convention from an Advanced-style file. Inorganic and practical-chemistry units lean heavily on direct NCERT-fact recall, which is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.

formulas: % composition = (mass of element/molar mass of compound) × 100
Molecular formula = n × empirical formula, n = molecular mass/empirical formula mass
methods: Identify the limiting reagent by comparing mole ratios to the balanced equation before computing product yield
traps: Using the given reagent's mass directly without checking which reactant is limiting
Confusing empirical formula mass with molecular mass
hard_archetypes: Multi-step stoichiometry problems combining limiting reagent with percentage yield
Back-calculating molecular formula from combustion-analysis data
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Direct mole-to-mass or mass-to-mole conversion questions are a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype — do not exclude these from a JEE Main bank.
out_of_scope: Formal treatment of significant figures/error propagation as a Chemistry-unit topic (this content was dropped from this unit in the 2025 rationalisation)

methods: Use the n=1 to n=2 (or similar) energy-level jump to compute the wavelength/frequency of emitted/absorbed radiation
traps: Forgetting the Z² scaling for hydrogen-like ions with Z>1
Assigning electron configurations without applying the extra stability of half-filled/fully-filled subshells (e.g. Cr, Cu)
hard_archetypes: Given two spectral lines' wavelengths, identify the transition and the element/ion
Anomalous electronic configuration questions for d-block exceptions (Cr, Cu, Mo)
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Direct quantum-number or orbital-shape identification questions are a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Full derivation of the Schrödinger wave equation

formulas: Hybridisation from steric number = (bond pairs + lone pairs)
methods: Count the steric number around the central atom first, then assign hybridisation and predict geometry from VSEPR
traps: Ignoring lone pairs when predicting molecular shape (e.g. confusing electron-pair geometry with molecular geometry)
Miscounting bonding vs antibonding electrons in MO diagrams for O2/N2-type molecules
hard_archetypes: Predicting the magnetic behaviour (paramagnetic/diamagnetic) of a diatomic species from its MO configuration
Ranking bond angles across a series of related molecules using VSEPR
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct 'identify the hybridisation/shape of X' question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Group theory / symmetry-based treatment of molecular orbitals

methods: Construct a Hess's-law thermochemical cycle to find an unknown enthalpy from given reaction enthalpies
traps: Sign errors in work done (w = -PΔV convention) for expansion vs compression
Forgetting to convert ΔH to ΔU (or vice versa) using Δn_g·RT for gas-phase reactions
hard_archetypes: Given several combustion/formation enthalpies, calculate the enthalpy of a target reaction via Hess's law
Determining spontaneity direction as a function of temperature using ΔH and ΔS signs
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. Direct Hess's-law addition/subtraction questions are a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Full Carnot-cycle efficiency derivation (removed from this unit in the 2025 rationalisation)

methods: Determine the van't Hoff factor from the degree of dissociation/association before applying a colligative-property formula
traps: Forgetting the van't Hoff factor i for ionic/associating solutes
Confusing molality (per kg solvent) with molarity (per litre solution) in colligative-property formulas
hard_archetypes: Given the observed and theoretical colligative-property values, back-calculate the degree of association/dissociation
Mixing two solutes to find the combined effect on freezing-point depression
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct single-formula colligative-property substitution is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Detailed vapour-pressure-composition curve derivations for strongly non-ideal systems beyond qualitative deviation

formulas: Ksp for a sparingly soluble salt
methods: Use the ICE-table approach for weak-acid/weak-base ionisation before computing equilibrium concentrations
traps: Neglecting the common-ion effect when a salt of the weak acid is already present
Confusing Ksp with solubility (s) — forgetting the stoichiometric exponents when relating them
hard_archetypes: Buffer-capacity/pH-after-addition-of-strong-acid-or-base problems
Simultaneous solubility-equilibrium problems with a common ion from two different salts
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct pH-of-a-weak-acid-solution question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Activity-coefficient-based (non-ideal) equilibrium treatments

concepts: Standard electrode potential and cell EMF
methods: Identify the cathode (reduction, higher E°) and anode (oxidation, lower E°) before writing the cell reaction and applying the Nernst equation
traps: Sign errors from swapping cathode and anode in the cell-potential formula
Forgetting to balance electrons before combining two half-reactions
hard_archetypes: Given concentration-dependent EMF data, determine an unknown concentration via the Nernst equation
Relating equilibrium constant, ΔG° and E°_cell in a single multi-formula problem
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct standard-EMF calculation from given electrode potentials is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Detailed industrial electrolysis cell-design specifics beyond qualitative dry-cell/lead-accumulator/fuel-cell working

concepts: Rate law and order of reaction
methods: Determine reaction order experimentally from a table of concentration-vs-rate data before writing the rate law
traps: Confusing order of reaction (empirical) with molecularity (theoretical, for elementary steps only)
Using the zero-order half-life formula for a first-order reaction or vice versa
hard_archetypes: Given rate data at two temperatures, calculate activation energy using the Arrhenius equation in logarithmic form
Determining the order of a reaction from a graphical (log-log) plot of rate vs concentration
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct first-order half-life or rate-constant-from-concentration-data question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Detailed collision-theory steric-factor derivations

C09.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
concepts: Periodic trends in atomic/ionic radius, ionisation enthalpy, electronegativity
formulas: No standard numerical formulas — trend-based, qualitative unit
methods: Cross-reference the element's block (s/p/d/f) and period position before predicting a periodic-trend-based property
traps: Applying the general 'ionisation enthalpy increases across a period' rule without accounting for known exceptions (e.g. Be>B, N>O)
Confusing electron gain enthalpy sign conventions
hard_archetypes: Ranking 4-5 elements/ions by ionic radius across both a period and a group simultaneously (isoelectronic species)
Identifying and explaining a specific periodic-trend anomaly
banned_easy_templates: A direct 'which of these has the highest/lowest [property]' recall question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype — do not exclude it.
out_of_scope: Detailed history of periodic-table development (Mendeleev vs modern law) beyond a passing statement

concepts: Anomalous behaviour of the first element in each p-block group
Preparation and properties of key p-block compounds (borax, diborane, ammonia, sulphuric acid)
formulas: No standard numerical formulas — descriptive/structural unit
methods: Match the given reaction/compound to its specific group-wise NCERT description before answering a properties-based question
traps: Confusing the acidic strength order of oxoacids of a given halogen/element
Mixing up structures of similarly-named oxoacids or interhalogen compounds
hard_archetypes: Multi-step conversion/preparation sequence questions for a p-block compound (e.g. borax to boric acid to B2O3)
Structure-based questions requiring identification of hybridisation in an interhalogen or xenon compound
banned_easy_templates: A direct 'name/identify this compound's use or preparation method' recall question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype — do not exclude it.
out_of_scope: Detailed industrial-scale manufacturing process parameters beyond the standard NCERT description

concepts: Variable oxidation states of transition metals
Colour and magnetic properties from unpaired d-electrons
formulas: Magnetic moment μ = √(n(n+2)) BM, where n = number of unpaired electrons
methods: Determine the electronic configuration of the relevant ion first, then count unpaired electrons before computing magnetic moment or predicting colour
traps: Forgetting that transition-metal ions (not neutral atoms) determine magnetic/colour properties in compounds
Confusing lanthanoid contraction's effect on the near-identical radii of 4d/5d elements of the same group
hard_archetypes: Given a set of transition-metal ions, rank them by magnetic moment or explain colour differences via d-d transitions
KMnO4/K2Cr2O7 balanced-equation and oxidation-state-change questions in redox titrations
banned_easy_templates: A direct 'what is the oxidation state of X in this compound' recall question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype — do not exclude it.
out_of_scope: Detailed crystal-field splitting energy (Δo/Δt) numerical calculations (this stays largely in C12's qualitative CFT scope)

concepts: Types of isomerism (ionisation, linkage, geometrical, optical)
Crystal field theory: high-spin vs low-spin, colour
formulas: CFSE (qualitative ranking, not full numerical treatment)
methods: Work out the oxidation state of the central metal from the overall charge and known ligand charges before naming the compound
traps: Confusing denticity of a ligand (e.g. treating EDTA as monodentate)
Missing geometrical (cis-trans) or optical isomerism possibilities in octahedral/square-planar complexes
hard_archetypes: Given a complex's formula, determine all possible isomers (geometrical + optical) and their count
Predict whether a complex is high-spin or low-spin and paramagnetic/diamagnetic using CFT
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct IUPAC-naming or coordination-number-identification question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Full ligand field theory / molecular orbital treatment of coordination compounds beyond basic CFT

C13.chapter: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
concepts: Purification techniques and their selection criteria
Detection of N/S/halogens via Lassaigne's test
Empirical formula from quantitative elemental analysis
formulas: % of element = (mass of element/mass of compound) × 100, from combustion/Carius/Kjeldahl data
methods: Match the compound's physical properties (volatility, thermal stability, mixture composition) to the appropriate purification technique before answering
traps: Confusing sublimation-suitable compounds with those needing distillation
Misreading Lassaigne's test colour results (Prussian blue for N, violet for S, etc.)
hard_archetypes: Given elemental percentage composition and molecular mass, derive the molecular formula
Multi-technique separation-sequence questions for a mixture of compounds with different properties
banned_easy_templates: A direct 'which technique purifies this compound' or 'what does this test detect' recall question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype — do not exclude it.
out_of_scope: Detailed instrumental spectroscopic characterisation methods (IR/NMR/mass spectrometry are not part of this unit)

C14.chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
concepts: Inductive, electromeric, resonance and hyperconjugation effects
formulas: No standard numerical formulas — conceptual/structural unit
methods: Identify all electron-donating/withdrawing groups attached to the reactive centre before ranking stability or acidity/basicity
traps: Confusing inductive effect (through sigma bonds) with resonance/electromeric effect (through pi systems)
Ranking carbocation stability without accounting for hyperconjugation from adjacent C-H bonds
hard_archetypes: Rank a series of 4-5 similar carbocations/carbanions/radicals by stability using combined inductive + resonance + hyperconjugation reasoning
Identify all types of isomerism possible for a given moderately complex structure
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct 'is this effect inductive or resonance' or basic nomenclature question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Advanced pericyclic-reaction electron-pushing mechanisms (outside NCERT scope)

concepts: Directive influence of substituents on benzene
formulas: No standard numerical formulas — mechanism/reaction-based unit
methods: Classify the substituent already on benzene as ortho/para-directing (activating) or meta-directing (deactivating) before predicting the product of a new substitution
traps: Applying Markovnikov's rule when peroxide is present (should use anti-Markovnikov/Kharasch addition instead)
Misidentifying a substituent's directing effect (e.g. halogens are deactivating yet ortho/para-directing)
hard_archetypes: Multi-step synthesis sequences from an alkane/alkene to a specific substituted arene, tracking each reagent's regiochemical effect
Ozonolysis-product-identification questions requiring reverse-engineering the parent alkene/alkyne structure
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct 'identify the major product of this addition/substitution' question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Detailed pericyclic/photochemical hydrocarbon reactions beyond NCERT scope

concepts: Nature of the C-X bond and reactivity trend
formulas: No standard numerical formulas — mechanism/fact-based unit
methods: Assess the substrate's carbon type (1°/2°/3°) and the nucleophile/solvent conditions before predicting SN1 vs SN2 pathway
traps: Assuming all nucleophilic substitutions on haloalkanes proceed by the same mechanism regardless of substrate/solvent
Confusing reactivity order of C-X bonds (C-F strongest/least reactive to C-I weakest/most reactive)
hard_archetypes: Given a specific substrate and nucleophile/solvent combination, predict whether SN1 or SN2 dominates and the stereochemical outcome (inversion vs racemisation)
banned_easy_templates: A direct 'which compound is used as X (e.g. DDT as a pesticide)' recall question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype — do not exclude it.
out_of_scope: Grignard-reagent organometallic chemistry in depth (touched on lightly under C17 instead)

concepts: Named reactions: aldol condensation, Cannizzaro, haloform, Reimer-Tiemann
Relative acidity of carboxylic acids vs phenols vs alcohols
formulas: No standard numerical formulas — mechanism/reaction-based unit
methods: Check for the presence of α-hydrogens first — their presence/absence determines whether aldol condensation or Cannizzaro reaction is possible
traps: Attempting Cannizzaro reaction on an aldehyde that has α-hydrogens (it requires no α-hydrogen)
Ranking acidity of substituted phenols/carboxylic acids without correctly weighing electron-withdrawing vs donating substituent effects
hard_archetypes: Multi-reagent synthesis sequence questions converting an alcohol to a specific carboxylic acid derivative via 3-4 steps
Distinguishing-test questions (iodoform, Tollens', Fehling's) requiring identification of which compounds give a positive result
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct 'name the product of this named reaction' question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Detailed asymmetric-synthesis/chiral-catalysis extensions of these reactions

concepts: Diazonium salt formation and synthetic utility
formulas: No standard numerical formulas — mechanism/reaction-based unit
methods: Weigh both the inductive (electron-donating alkyl groups) and steric/solvation effects together when ranking amine basicity in aqueous solution, rather than using alkyl-group count alone
traps: Ranking amine basicity purely by alkyl-substitution count without accounting for steric hindrance and solvation in water
Confusing the conditions/temperature required for diazonium salt stability (must be below 5°C)
hard_archetypes: Given a set of substituted anilines/amines, rank them by basicity accounting for both electronic and steric effects
Multi-step synthesis using a diazonium-salt intermediate (Sandmeyer, Gattermann reactions) to reach a target aromatic product
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct 1°/2°/3°-amine identification or basic-nomenclature question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Detailed diazo-coupling dye-chemistry beyond the basic synthetic-utility mention

concepts: DNA vs RNA composition and base-pairing
formulas: No standard numerical formulas — descriptive/qualitative unit
methods: Match the described molecule's functional groups/linkages (glycosidic, peptide, phosphodiester) to the correct biomolecule class before answering
traps: Confusing the four structural levels of proteins (e.g. attributing quaternary-structure features to tertiary structure)
Mixing up the nitrogenous bases/sugar unique to DNA (thymine, deoxyribose) vs RNA (uracil, ribose)
hard_archetypes: Given a description of a protein's denaturation conditions, identify which structural level is disrupted
Distinguish reducing vs non-reducing sugars from their glycosidic-linkage description (e.g. sucrose vs maltose)
banned_easy_templates: A direct 'which vitamin deficiency causes X' or 'is this sugar reducing/non-reducing' recall question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype — do not exclude it.
out_of_scope: Detailed enzyme-kinetics (Michaelis-Menten) treatment

concepts: Qualitative salt analysis: cation/anion confirmatory tests
Volumetric titration principles and indicator choice
Preparation of specific inorganic/organic compounds listed in NCERT practicals
methods: Match the described precipitate colour/gas evolved/flame-test result to the specific cation or anion from the standard NCERT qualitative-analysis scheme
traps: Confusing similarly-coloured precipitates from different cations (e.g. white precipitates of several salts)
Picking the wrong indicator for a given acid-base titration type (strong-strong vs weak-strong)
hard_archetypes: Given a sequence of observations from an unknown-salt analysis, identify the cation and anion present
Multi-step preparation-procedure questions requiring the correct order of reagents for one of the listed NCERT preparations
banned_easy_templates: A direct 'name this test's positive-result observation' recall question is acceptable and common for this unit — do not exclude it (unlike other JEE Main units, pure recall is a legitimate archetype here).
out_of_scope: Any salt or preparation not among the specific NCERT-listed cations/anions/compounds for this unit; insoluble salts are explicitly excluded
